key_insight: Entropy-driven multicomponent B-site substitution in BF-BT ceramics creates a more pseudocubic, relaxor-like microstructure that suppresses hysteresis and boosts breakdown strength for much higher energy storage.
engineering_relevance: This suggests entropy engineering is a practical materials design strategy for lead-free dielectric capacitors needing high recoverable energy density and reliable ultra-high-field operation.
method: Added a high-entropy perovskite oxide, BaTi0.2Zr0.2Sn0.2Hf0.2Nb0.1Sc0.1O3, into the BF-BT matrix
Used multicomponent B-site substitution to induce lattice distortion, grain refinement, and relaxor behavior
Leveraged microstructural heterogeneity to improve field uniformity and delay dielectric breakdown
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a maximum breakdown strength of 840 kV/cm and a recoverable energy density of 10.55 J/cm3, indicating strong dielectric performance gains.
watch_item: The reported performance is from bulk ceramic samples, so translating these results into scalable devices will require verifying processing consistency, long-term reliability, and field cycling stability.
paper_title: Entropy engineering of BF-BT-based high-entropy ceramics for ultra-high energy storage performance
